_doc: NPC_AI_SPEC §6 (Perception) + §3.3 (Belief) — every tunable the vision
sensor, the hearing sensor, belief decay and threat derivation read.
§12's rule applies: nothing in src/ai/perception/*.ts hardcodes a number
that belongs here.
The spec gives almost NO defaults for §6 (only the 0.05 prune floor, the
200-600ms reaction window, the ~1.5s worst-case confidence ramp and the
0.3 threat lerp). Everything else below was chosen against ranges this
game has already tuned, not picked at random — each one carries its
reference point so a later tuning pass knows what it is trading against:
INTERACT_RANGE 3.4      game/data/world.ts — arm's reach
NOTICE_RANGE 5          ai/actions/notice.ts — 'right next to you'
MELEE_RANGE 1.8         components/world/Defenders.tsx
BOW_RANGE 16            components/world/Defenders.tsx
RANGED_RANGE 14         components/combat/Enemies.tsx (crossbow bandit)
ENGAGE_RADIUS 22        Defenders.tsx — a SWORN defender's watch
SCOUT_EYES 30           Defenders.tsx — a scout order, +Wit
enemy chase leash 26    Enemies.tsx
nearDistance 15         ai/config/lod.json — 'close enough to matter'
`updateHz` is deliberately absent (§6.1 asks for 4-6 Hz): perception runs
at the agent's OWN lod.json `perceiveHz` (A 6 / B 4 / C 2 / D off), which
already sits in that band. A second copy here would be one more pair of
numbers that has to agree by hand, and this project has already been bitten
by exactly that (PHASE_STATUS.md §2's tier-B window-radius gap).
fov is the FULL cone angle in radians; 2.0 rad = 114.6 degrees, roughly
human comfortable binocular vision. range 16 = BOW_RANGE: a villager
notices a raider at the distance a bow can answer it, but well inside
the 22m a sworn defender is paid to watch — the farmer is not the
lookout, and it should read that way. peripheralRange 6 is 360 degrees:
one notch past notice.ts's own NOTICE_RANGE 5, so something at your
shoulder registers no matter which way you are facing.
rampSecondsFar is §6.1's own number ('a target at the edge of the cone
at max range should take ~1.5s to reach full confidence'); rampSecondsNear
is the same ramp at zero distance, lerped between by distance fraction.
§6.1 also wants a target-SIZE term — omitted deliberately: every
perceivable entity in this game is the same minifig scale, and
EnemyData.scale (game/combat.ts) is an HP multiplier, not a physical one.
losChecksPerTick is §6.1's 'max 4 raycasts per agent per tick, round-robin
the rest', kept verbatim even though the check is a nav-grid march rather
than a THREE.Raycaster (see VisionSensor.ts's header for that divergence).
losSampleStep is in world units — half a nav cell (navgrid.json cellSize
1.0), so no single blocked cell can be stepped over.
§6.2: the world emits {position, loudness, type, sourceId} and the
manager dispatches to agents within `loudness * falloff`.
radiusPerLoudness IS that falloff: a loudness-1.0 event carries 24m,
between the defender's 22m watch and the mob's 26m chase leash — a
pitched fight at the edge of the homestead is heard across it.
`loudness` is the authored table every real emitter reads (exported as
SOUND_LOUDNESS from perception/sounds.ts; call sites are in
game/combat.ts, beside the audio.play they already fire):
playerStruck 0.9 -> ~22m, the loudest thing in the game
meleeHit     0.75 -> ~18m, a running fight
boltHit      0.5 -> ~12m, one thud, not an exchange
fuzzRadius is §6.2's 'offset by a few metres so NPCs investigate an area
rather than walking to the exact source'. confidence 0.35 is the CEILING
a heard-but-unseen belief can reach — it sits above `belief.noticedAt`
(0.2), which is the deliberate line: hearing a fight is enough to
register and make an agent uneasy (up to ~0.35 threat at close range),
and nowhere near what a confirmed sighting produces (confidence ramps to
1.0). Sound raises an eyebrow; sight makes you run. The SIZE of that gap
is set by noticedAt, not by this number — see `belief._doc` for why a
one-shot sound needs ~2.2s above the threshold and only got 0.6s when the
two were 0.05 apart.
The player's own footsteps are the one continuous source (a sprint is
audible, a walk is not): sprintSpeed 5 is the exact threshold
PlayerAvatar.tsx already uses to switch to anim_c_run, and footstepLoudness
0.33 x 24m = ~8m of earshot — closer than sight range, which is what makes
hearing a distinct cue rather than a worse copy of vision.
§3.3: `confidence *= Math.exp(-decayRate * dt)`, prune below 0.05.
decayPerSec 0.25 means a belief that peaked at 1.0 falls to the 0.05
prune floor in ln(20)/0.25 = ~12s — long enough that an NPC keeps
reacting to the bandit that just ducked behind the barn, short enough
that it forgets a lone wanderer rather than staying rattled all day.
noticedAt is §3.3's 'noticed threshold' — the confidence at which a
belief starts counting toward threat at all. It has to sit UNDER
`hearing.confidence` (0.35) or a sound-only belief could never cross it
and the whole hearing sensor would be inert, with §6.3's 'hostile belief
count' input only ever seeing things already in plain sight.
How FAR under is the load-bearing part, and 0.3 was too close. A one-shot
sound pins a belief at exactly 0.35 and it then decays, so the belief is
above the threshold for only ln(0.35/noticedAt)/decayPerSec seconds — at
0.3 that is 0.62s, and §3.3's own per-agent reaction delay (0.2-0.6s,
rolled at spawn) ate most or all of it: two identical live runs of 'one
combat sound at 5m' gave threat 0.23 and threat 0.00, decided purely by
which reaction time that agent happened to roll. 0.2 gives 2.24s of
window instead — more than three times the worst-case delay plus a think
period — so a heard fight reliably registers on every agent rather than
on roughly half of them. It stays well clear of the 0.05 prune floor, and
the ceiling a heard belief can reach is unchanged (0.35), so hearing
still cannot push threat past take_cover's own 0.4 entry gate: that
loop-freedom margin (combat.json's `cover._doc`) is untouched by this.
reactionMin/MaxSec is §3.3's 200-600ms reaction delay, rolled once
per agent at spawn so two villagers never flinch in lockstep.
visibleGraceSec is how long `isVisibleNow` survives without a refresh —
comfortably longer than the slowest perceive period (tier C, 0.5s) plus
a round-robin deferral or two, so §6.1's LOS budget cannot make a target
in plain sight flicker. See Belief.ts's decayBeliefs for why expiry lives
there rather than in the sensor.
§6.3: derived once per think tick from beliefs, then smoothed so it
cannot spike and flip the action mid-swing. The spec's own figure is a
'lerp toward the target by 0.3' PER TICK — which would make threat rise
20x faster on a tier-A agent (10 Hz) than a tier-D one (0.5 Hz) purely
because of its LOD tier. Re-expressed here as a time constant instead:
0.3 per 0.1s tick is exp(-0.1/tau) = 0.7, i.e. tau = 0.28s. Same feel at
tier A, tier-independent everywhere else — the same correction phase 1
already made for needs decay (decay by real elapsed time, not per tick).
closeDistance 4 / falloffDistance 16: a hostile inside 4m contributes
its full confidence to threat, falling linearly to nothing at the edge of
sight (vision.range). extraPerHostile is the §6.3 'hostile belief count'
term — each ADDITIONAL noticed hostile adds this much, so three raiders
at the fence are worse than one.
damageMemorySec/damageWeight are §6.3's 'time since last damage' term,
reading bb.lastDamageAt. Written for real as of Wave 21 (2026-08-28) —
Enemies.tsx's villagerTarget branch calls reportAgentDamaged() when an
ordinary villager who chose to fight (engage_threat_villager) takes a
hit. Until then nothing wrote this field, and that was not an oversight:
an ordinary villager could not be damaged at all before that wave
(Enemies.tsx only ever targeted the player, sworn defenders via
defenderState, and keep pieces) — the term was implemented and inert on
purpose, so phase 7's combat pass would have a real seam to write into.
See perception/Senses.ts's reportAgentDamaged() and
actions/engageThreatVillager.ts for the real caller.
